issues.legal_issue: A later written acknowledgment and the surrounding evidence may establish that a debt and deposit of title deeds were intended to create a mortgage, even where the parties had contemplated a formal mortgage deed.
material_facts: The borrower received advances under several promissory notes, and the lender possessed title deeds relating to the borrower’s properties.
A memorandum executed after the alleged deposit acknowledged the debt and expressly recorded that the title deeds had been deposited with intent to create security.
The borrower did not deny the allegations in the suit and was not examined to explain the memorandum.
The lender and witnesses gave evidence consistent with the acknowledgment; the court found that their evidence did not displace it.
issues.conclusion: The evidence established that the parties intended the title deeds to secure the debt; an intention to execute a formal mortgage later did not negate an existing mortgage by deposit of title deeds.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a mortgage by deposit of title deeds requires a debt, deposit of title deeds, and an intention that the deeds secure the debt. Intention is a question of fact determined from the evidence; there is no presumption of law that mere deposit creates a mortgage, although an inference may be drawn under section 114 of the Evidence Act. A contemplated formal mortgage does not, by itself, rule out an immediate security. The Court discussed Norris v. Wilkinson, Keys v. Williams, Dayal Jairaj v. Jivraj Ratansi, Jaitha Bhima v. Haji Abdul Vyad Cosman, Behram Bashid Irani v. Sorabji Rustomji Elavia, and V.E.R.M.A.R. Chettyar Firm v. Ma Joo Teen.

rule.if: mortgage_enforcement_proceeding and loan_debt_exists and title_documents_held_for_transaction and later_written_acknowledgment_recites_security_intention

predicates.mortgage_enforcement_proceeding: The proceeding seeks enforcement of a claimed mortgage by deposit of title deeds.
predicates.loan_debt_exists: The borrower received money from the lender that remained owing.
predicates.title_documents_held_for_transaction: The lender held title documents relating to the borrower’s property in connection with the lending transaction.
predicates.later_written_acknowledgment_recites_sec: A later written acknowledgment records that the title documents were deposited with the intention of securing the debt.

issues.definition: When a mortgage-enforcement proceeding involves an existing debt, title documents held in connection with the transaction, and a later written acknowledgment reciting security intent, the security intention is established.

issues.legal_issue: A debtor may constructively deposit title deeds by agreeing that documents already held by the creditor as the debtor’s agent are thereafter held as security.
material_facts: The title deeds were physically held by the lender in the relevant city before the parties agreed to treat them as security.
The lender initially held the deeds as agent for the borrower, rather than in the lender’s own right.
The borrower and lender met while the deeds were in the lender’s possession, and the borrower agreed that the lender should hold them as security for the advances.
The court found that the deeds were physically handed over as security, and held that constructive delivery would suffice even if that formality had not occurred.
issues.conclusion: The agreement changed the character of the lender’s possession and constituted constructive delivery of the title deeds, satisfying the delivery requirement for a mortgage by deposit of title deeds.
issues.legal_principle: Section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 does not require physical delivery in a particular form where the creditor already holds the documents. The court asks whether, in substance, the parties agreed that the creditor or agent would hold the documents as security. The Court relied on the substance-over-form reasoning in Whitbread, Ex Parte, and distinguished In re Beetham, Ex Parte Broderick, which concerned part performance of an oral promise and did not decide the constructive-delivery point.

rule.if: mortgage_enforcement_proceeding and loan_debt_exists and creditor_holds_documents_as_debtor_agent and documents_are_held_in_required_city and debtor_agrees_to_retain_documents_as_security

predicates.mortgage_enforcement_proceeding: The proceeding seeks enforcement of a claimed mortgage by deposit of title deeds.
predicates.loan_debt_exists: The borrower owes money advanced by the creditor.
predicates.creditor_holds_documents_as_debtor_agent: The creditor already possesses the debtor’s title documents but holds them on the debtor’s behalf rather than as security.
predicates.documents_are_held_in_required_city: The documents are held in a city where the law permits this form of mortgage to be created.
predicates.debtor_agrees_to_retain_documents_as_sec: The debtor agrees that the creditor will thereafter hold the documents to secure the debt.

issues.definition: If a creditor holding the debtor’s documents as agent in a legally permitted city agrees with the debtor to hold them as security for an existing debt, that agreement amounts to constructive delivery.

issues.legal_issue: A written agreement expressing an intention that title deeds already in the creditor’s possession secure an existing debt may itself create a mortgage from the agreement’s execution, even if no earlier mortgage was created.
material_facts: The borrower owed the lender money, and the title deeds were in the lender’s possession when the memorandum was executed.
The memorandum was executed after the alleged original deposit and recorded the borrower’s intention that the title deeds secure the advances.
The memorandum was registered later, but the court found that registration gave it effect from its execution date under section 47 of the Registration Act.
The court held that, even if no mortgage had been created on the earlier alleged deposit date, the necessary elements were present when the memorandum was executed.
issues.conclusion: In the alternative, the mortgage was created from the date the memorandum was executed, even if no mortgage had arisen on the earlier alleged date.
issues.legal_principle: Section 58(f) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 requires a debt, delivery of title deeds (including constructive delivery), and an intention to secure the debt. Where the creditor already possesses the deeds, the debtor’s agreement that they are to secure an existing debt supplies the necessary constructive delivery and intention. Under section 47 of the Registration Act, a registered document operates from the time it would have commenced to operate if registration had not been required. The Court’s discussion of constructive delivery in Whitbread, Ex Parte supports this approach.

rule.if: mortgage_enforcement_proceeding and no_earlier_mortgage_created and loan_debt_exists and creditor_possesses_title_documents and executed_agreement_expresses_security_intention

predicates.mortgage_enforcement_proceeding: The proceeding seeks enforcement of a claimed mortgage by deposit of title deeds.
predicates.no_earlier_mortgage_created: The evidence does not establish that a mortgage was created on the earlier alleged occasion.
predicates.loan_debt_exists: The borrower owes money already advanced by the creditor.
predicates.creditor_possesses_title_documents: The creditor has the debtor’s title documents when the agreement is executed.
predicates.executed_agreement_expresses_security_in: The debtor executes an agreement expressing that the documents are to secure the existing debt.

issues.definition: If no earlier mortgage was created but an existing debt, the creditor’s possession of the title documents, and an executed agreement expressing security intent are present, the mortgage is created from execution of that agreement.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgage by deposit of title deeds takes priority over a mortgage deed subsequently executed and registered over the same property.
material_facts: The court found that the lender’s mortgage by deposit of title deeds was created before the competing mortgage deed was executed.
The competing mortgage deed related to the same property and was executed and registered after the earlier mortgage arose.
The memorandum acknowledging the earlier mortgage was registered after its execution, and the court held that it took effect from its execution date.
issues.conclusion: The mortgage by deposit of title deeds had priority over the subsequent mortgage deed.
issues.legal_principle: The proviso to section 48 of the Registration Act, 1908 provides that a mortgage by deposit of title deeds as defined in section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 takes effect against a subsequently executed and registered mortgage deed relating to the same property. Under section 47 of the Registration Act, a registered document takes effect from the time it would have commenced to operate if registration had not been required.

predicates.competing_mortgage_priority_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the relative priority of competing security interests over property.
predicates.title_deed_mortgage_created_first: A mortgage by deposit of title deeds was created before the competing mortgage deed.
predicates.later_registered_mortgage_deed_covers_sa: A mortgage deed was subsequently executed and registered over the same property.

issues.definition: In a priority proceeding, an earlier mortgage by deposit of title deeds has priority when a later registered mortgage deed covers the same property.
